title: Comparative study on pollution characteristics of heavy metals and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in coking solid wastes
content:
Abstract

Coking, an important method of coal utilization, inevitably produces various solid wastes, including coke powder (CP), tar residue (TR), oil-washing sludge (OS), and coking sludge (CS). Although previous studies have focused on the pollutant characteristics of individual wastes such as CP and TR, systematic comparisons of heavy metals and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) across different types of waste remain insufficiently explored. This study systematically investigates the pollution characteristics of heavy metals and PAHs in these coking solid wastes. The results indicate that the different kinds of coking solid wastes have irregular shapes with small amounts of micropores on the particle surfaces. The different kinds of coking solid wastes contain varying amounts of heavy metals, including As, Zn, Cu, Cr, Ni, and Cd; and the ecological risk of heavy metals is TR > CS > CP > OS. In contrast, the pollution characteristic of PAHs in coking solid wastes is more serious than that of heavy metals; 16 kinds of PAHs with controlled priority of US Environmental Protection Agency are detected in the different kinds of coking solid wastes, especially about 2–3 ring compounds; the ecotoxicity and carcinogenicity of coking solid wastes correspond to the levels of ΣPAHs in coking solid wastes. This study aims to provide a scientific foundation for the resource utilization and safe disposal of coking solid waste in the coking industry.
